title: Sentinel Evidence Locker
intro: Every quarter Sentinel has to prove its controls operated: access reviews ran, backups restored, changes were approved. The auditor does not accept 'we did it' - only evidence, collected on time, unaltered, attested by the right person, kept on schedule. You are going to build the audit automation: request the evidence each quarter, record it so it can never be edited, decide whether it is sufficient, track what is not, and assemble the package. Then it meets a quarter where the evidence is true but too old, attested to the wrong period, corrected, and - for one control - never sent.

world.oneLiner: Sentinel Health proves every quarter that its security controls operated, with evidence that is fresh, unaltered and attested, assembled into an audit package the auditor can rely on.

roles.name: Compliance Analyst
roles.does: Runs the quarterly collection and hears when evidence is missing.

roles.name: Control Owners
roles.does: Produce the evidence for their controls and attest to it - addressed by control id, like 'owner of AC-2'.

roles.name: Internal Auditor
roles.does: Countersigns attested evidence and issues findings.

roles.name: CISO
roles.does: Owns the control catalog and the retention schedule.

roles.name: Audit DL
roles.does: The distribution list that receives the quarterly package.

world.deliverable: a complete audit package at the end of every quarter
world.clock: Day 1 of the quarter: requests go to every control owner. Through the quarter: evidence arrives and is judged as it lands. Last day: the package flow checks every control is covered and sends the package.
world.stakes: Get it wrong and the auditor finds evidence that was quietly edited, a control that was 'proven' with last year's report, or a control nobody collected anything for.

sources.label: Evidence Submissions
sources.description: A control owner's evidence: which control, which period, when it was collected, its hash, and who attests to what.

stores.label: Control Catalog
stores.description: Every control Sentinel must prove: its owner and how many days its evidence stays fresh.

stores.label: Quarter
stores.description: Which quarter this is, and the day number it ends on.

stores.label: Evidence Requests
stores.description: This quarter's asks, one per control.

stores.label: Evidence Records
stores.description: Every piece of evidence ever received, with its hash. Rows are added, never edited; a correction is a new row that names what it supersedes.

stores.label: Findings
stores.description: Controls whose evidence fell short this quarter, with the reason, an owner and a deadline.

stores.label: Retention Schedule
stores.description: How many years each class of record is kept, by regulation.

stores.label: Evidence Calendar
stores.description: When each control's evidence expires and must be collected again.

stores.label: Audit Archive
stores.description: Every quarterly package, kept for the years the schedule says.

flows.name: Quarter start
flows.description: Runs on day 1 of the quarter: ask every owner for evidence.

flows.name: Quarter end
flows.description: Runs on the last day of the quarter: check coverage, assemble, send.

days.label: Q1 - three controls, three clean submissions
days.description: Three controls in the catalog. Every owner sends fresh evidence for Q1, attests to Q1, and the Internal Auditor countersigns.

days.label: Q2 - true but old, the wrong period, and a correction
days.description: AC-2's owner sends the review from 110 days ago - real, but past its 90-day window. CM-3's owner attests to Q1 by mistake. CP-9's owner sends a restore log, then a corrected one.

evidence-submissions.note: restore test log - corrected, first upload was truncated

days.label: Q3 - one owner never answers
days.description: AC-2 and CM-3 arrive clean. Nothing arrives for CP-9. Nothing fails; the package just has two controls in it.

builds.title: Ask for the evidence
builds.brief: On day 1, send every control owner a precise request.
builds.goal: The catalog lists every control Sentinel must prove and who owns it. On the first day of the quarter, turn each control into a request: which control, which period, by when - and tell the owner.
builds.outcome: Every control in the catalog has a request for this quarter, and the owners are told.
constraints: One request per control, from the catalog - do not type control ids.
The period and the as-of day come from the Quarter table.
Add or replace by controlId.

hints.question: If the CISO adds a control next quarter, what should your flow have to change?
hints.nudge: Lookup Quarter where key = 'current' (q); Lookup Control Catalog, all rows (controls); For each over controls: Transform period = parent.q.period, asOfDay = parent.q.asOfDay; Store into Evidence Requests (add or replace by controlId); Send to Control Owners.
steps: Add a Lookup on Quarter where key = 'current'. Name it q.
Add a Lookup on Control Catalog, all rows. Name it controls. Add a For each over controls.
Inside: Transform period = parent.q.period, asOfDay = parent.q.asOfDay.
Inside: Store into Evidence Requests, add or replace by controlId; Send to Control Owners ('{{controlId}} evidence for {{period}} due by day {{asOfDay}}').
Run it.

checks.why: No requests, no evidence, no package.
checks.label: The request flow runs without failing

checks.why: Three controls, three asks.
checks.label: Three requests, one per control

checks.why: A request without a period is not precise enough to attest to.
checks.label: AC-2's request is for Q1, as of day 90

checks.why: The owner of CP-9 has to hear about CP-9.
checks.label: The owners are told (CP-9 named)

builds.title: Record the evidence
builds.brief: When evidence arrives, record it with its hash - the record is the product.
builds.goal: An owner's submission is the evidence: its control, its period, when it was collected, its hash, who attests. Look the control up, and record the submission in Evidence Records.
builds.outcome: Every submission is in Evidence Records with its hash and attestation, keyed by control.
constraints: Attach the control from the catalog as control.
Keep the hash exactly as received.
One record per control for now - add or replace by controlId.

hints.question: What does the auditor need to see to believe the access review happened?
hints.nudge: Trigger on Evidence Submissions; a Lookup on Control Catalog by controlId (control); a Store into Evidence Records, add or replace by controlId.
steps: Open the Evidence arrives flow and connect its Trigger to Evidence Submissions.
Add a Lookup on Control Catalog where controlId = controlId. Name it control.
Add a Store into Evidence Records, add or replace if it exists, same row when controlId. Run it.

checks.why: Evidence that fails to record did not happen, as far as the auditor is concerned.
checks.label: The evidence flow runs without failing

checks.why: The hash is what proves the file was not changed later.
checks.label: AC-2's evidence is recorded with hash h-ac2-q1

checks.why: Every control's evidence is on record.
checks.label: Three records

builds.title: Attest and decide
builds.brief: Attested and countersigned evidence passes; anything else is a finding with an owner and a deadline.
builds.goal: Evidence is sufficient when the owner attested to it and the Internal Auditor countersigned. Capture the countersign, decide, and log the outcome either way: a pass, or a finding that names the owner and gives them 30 days.
builds.outcome: Every submission ends in the Pass Log or in Findings with a reason, an owner and a deadline; the countersign is captured.
constraints: The countersign is an Approval from the Internal Auditor, captured on the record.
A finding always carries reason, owner and deadlineDay (as-of day plus 30).
Passing controls are logged too.

hints.question: Who has to say yes before AC-2 counts as proven, and where is that recorded?
hints.nudge: Lookup Evidence Requests by controlId (request); Approval from Internal Auditor; Transform attested = len(attestedBy) > 0; Condition attested and approval.outcome == countersigned: YES lane Store into Pass Log; NO lane Transform reason, owner = control.owner, deadlineDay = request.asOfDay + 30; Store into Findings; Send to Control Owners.
steps: After the control Lookup, add a Lookup on Evidence Requests where controlId = controlId. Name it request.
Add an Approval from Internal Auditor about 'countersign {{controlId}}'.
Add a Transform: attested = len(attestedBy) > 0.

Add a Condition: attested == true AND approval.outcome == countersigned. YES lane: Store into Pass Log. NO lane: Transform reason = 'not attested or not countersigned', owner = control.owner, deadlineDay = request.asOfDay + 30; Store into Findings; Send to Control Owners ('Finding on {{controlId}}: {{reason}}').
Run it.

checks.why: A clean quarter: three passes on record, not just an absence of findings.
checks.label: All three controls pass

checks.why: The countersign is the auditor's signature; it lives on the record.
checks.label: The Internal Auditor's countersign is captured on S-101

checks.why: No findings on a clean quarter.
checks.label: No findings

builds.title: The package
builds.brief: On the last day, assemble the package and send it to the auditors.
builds.goal: The package is the quarter: every record with its hash, every pass, every finding, and how long it will all be kept. Count, look up the retention, compose, send to the Audit DL, archive.
builds.outcome: The Audit DL receives the package listing every record and finding; the archive row carries the retention years.
constraints: Name the counts passes and findings.
Retention comes from the Retention Schedule for record class 'evidence'.

hints.question: What will the auditor open first?
hints.nudge: All-rows Lookups on Evidence Records (records), Pass Log (passed) and Findings (open); Lookup Retention Schedule where recordClass = 'evidence' (retention); Transform passes = len(passed), findings = len(open), retainYears = retention.years; Compose; Send to Audit DL; Store into Audit Archive.
steps: Open the Quarter end flow.
Lookups, all rows: Evidence Records as records, Pass Log as passed, Findings as open.
Lookup Retention Schedule where recordClass = 'evidence'. Name it retention.
Transform: passes = len(passed), findings = len(open), retainYears = retention.years.
Compose package with the counts, {{#each records}}- {{controlId}} {{period}} {{hash}}{{/each}} and {{#each open}}- {{controlId}}: {{reason}}{{/each}}.
Send to Audit DL with {{package}}; Store into Audit Archive.

checks.why: The package states what passed.
checks.label: The package counts 3 passes

checks.why: The regulation sets the floor; the package carries it.
checks.label: Retention is 7 years, from the schedule

checks.why: The auditor checks hashes, not summaries.
checks.label: The Audit DL receives the package with the hashes

checks.why: The archived package is what the next audit reads.
checks.label: The package is archived

builds.title: When does it expire?
builds.brief: Every piece of evidence expires. Put the date on the calendar.
builds.goal: Proof goes stale: an access review is good for 90 days, a restore test for 180. After the package, compute when each control's evidence expires and put it on the Evidence Calendar, so next quarter's requests know what to ask for.
builds.outcome: The Evidence Calendar holds each control's nextDueDay, from the record's collection day plus the control's freshness window.
constraints: nextDueDay = collectedDay + the control's freshnessDays.
One row per control in the calendar.

hints.question: AC-2 was collected on day 75 and is good for 90 days. When must it be collected again?
hints.nudge: After the archive Store, a For each over records; inside: Lookup Control Catalog by controlId (control); Transform nextDueDay = collectedDay + control.freshnessDays; Store into Evidence Calendar, add or replace by controlId.
steps: After the archive Store, add a For each over records.

Inside: Lookup Control Catalog where controlId = controlId (control); Transform nextDueDay = collectedDay + control.freshnessDays; Store into Evidence Calendar, add or replace if it exists, same row when controlId.
Run it and open the Evidence Calendar.

checks.why: 75 + 90: the day the review stops being proof.
checks.label: AC-2 expires on day 165
CP-9 expires on day 210

checks.why: One date per control.
checks.label: One calendar row per control

builds.title: Q2: true, but too old - and the wrong period
builds.brief: Stale evidence fails even when true. So does an attestation to the wrong period.
builds.goal: AC-2's owner sent the review they ran 110 days ago; CM-3's owner attested to Q1 on a Q2 submission. Run your Q1 flow: both pass. Sufficient means fresh - collected within the control's window as of the quarter end - and attested to THIS period. Add both tests to the decision.
builds.outcome: Stale evidence and an attestation to the wrong period are findings with the reason named; fresh, correctly attested evidence still passes.
constraints: ageDays = the request's asOfDay minus collectedDay; fresh when ageDays <= control.freshnessDays.
attested means attestedPeriod == period, not just a name.
Each finding names its reason: stale, or wrong period.

hints.question: The access review is real. Why does the auditor reject it?
hints.nudge: Transform ageDays = request.asOfDay - collectedDay, fresh = ageDays <= control.freshnessDays, attested = attestedPeriod == period; the Condition becomes fresh AND attested AND countersigned; the NO lane's reason = if(fresh == false, 'stale evidence', 'attested to the wrong period').
steps: Run first and read the Pass Log.
Change the Transform: ageDays = request.asOfDay - collectedDay, fresh = ageDays <= control.freshnessDays, attested = attestedPeriod == period.
Change the Condition: fresh == true AND attested == true AND approval.outcome == countersigned.
In the NO lane, reason = if(fresh == false, 'stale evidence', 'attested to the wrong period'). Run again.

checks.why: 110 days old against a 90-day window: not proof of this quarter.
checks.label: AC-2 is a finding: stale evidence

checks.why: An attestation to Q1 proves nothing about Q2.
checks.label: CM-3 is a finding: attested to the wrong period

checks.why: A finding without an owner and a date is a note nobody acts on.
checks.label: AC-2's finding has an owner and a deadline (day 210)

checks.why: CP-9's evidence is fresh and attested to Q2
checks.label: CP-9 is not a finding

builds.title: Q2: the correction
builds.brief: Evidence is never edited. A correction is a new record that names what it replaces.
builds.goal: CP-9's owner sent a truncated log, then a corrected one. Run your flow and open Evidence Records: the first upload is gone, replaced. That is an edit, and an auditor will ask what else was edited. Records are added, never replaced: the correction is a new row with a version and the hash it supersedes.
builds.outcome: Both CP-9 submissions are in Evidence Records; the correction carries version 2 and supersedes the first hash; nothing was overwritten.
constraints: Add, never replace.
Look up the prior record for the control AND the period; version = prior.version + 1 (or 1); supersedes = prior.hash.
Every other control still gets version 1.

hints.question: After the correction, how many CP-9 records should the auditor be able to see?
hints.nudge: Before the record Store, Lookup Evidence Records where controlId = controlId and period = period (prior); Transform version = coalesce(prior.version, 0) + 1, supersedes = coalesce(prior.hash, ''); change the Store to add a new row.
steps: Run first and count CP-9 rows in Evidence Records.
Before the record Store, add a Lookup on Evidence Records where controlId = controlId and period = period. Name it prior.
Add a Transform: version = coalesce(prior.version, 0) + 1, supersedes = coalesce(prior.hash, '').
Change the Store into Evidence Records to 'add a new row'. Run again.

checks.why: Both uploads exist; the auditor can see the correction happened.
checks.label: Both CP-9 Q2 submissions are on record

checks.why: The correction says what it corrects.
checks.label: The correction is version 2 and supersedes h-cp9-q2a

checks.why: The original is untouched.
checks.label: The original is still there, version 1

builds.title: Q3: nothing arrived for CP-9
builds.brief: A control with no evidence is a finding, not an omission.
builds.goal: AC-2 and CM-3 arrive clean. Nothing arrives for CP-9, so nothing runs for it, and the package lists two controls as if the catalog had two. Before assembling, check every control in the catalog has evidence for this period; a control with none is a finding with an owner and a deadline, and the Compliance Analyst is told.
builds.outcome: A control with no evidence this quarter appears in Findings as 'no evidence' with its owner, the Compliance Analyst is told, and the package counts it.
constraints: Check the catalog, not the records - the records cannot tell you what is missing.
Match on control AND period.
The finding has an owner and a deadline like any other.

hints.question: How many controls are in the catalog? How many are in the package?
hints.nudge: At the start of Quarter end: Lookup Quarter (q); Lookup Control Catalog, all rows (controls); For each over controls: Lookup Evidence Records where controlId = controlId and period = parent.q.period (evidence); Condition evidence missing: YES lane Transform reason = 'no evidence', deadlineDay = parent.q.asOfDay + 30; Store into Findings; Send to Compliance Analyst. Then the counts as before.
steps: Run first and read the package.
At the start of the flow: Lookup Quarter where key = 'current' (q); Lookup Control Catalog, all rows (controls); For each over controls.

Inside: Lookup Evidence Records where controlId = controlId and period = parent.q.period (evidence); Condition evidence missing; YES lane: Transform reason = 'no evidence', deadlineDay = parent.q.asOfDay + 30; Store into Findings; Send to Compliance Analyst ('No evidence for {{controlId}} in {{parent.q.period}}').
Keep the counts and the package after the loop. Run again.

checks.why: Silence is the most dangerous gap: nothing failed, so nothing was logged.
checks.label: CP-9 is a finding: no evidence, owner named, deadline day 300

checks.why: Someone has to chase the owner before the package ships.
checks.label: The Compliance Analyst is told

checks.why: The package counts the gap.
checks.label: The package counts 1 finding

checks.why: The two clean controls still pass.
checks.label: The package counts 2 passes
